NC500: Clockwise or Anticlockwise?

The North Coast 500 is Scotland's answer to Route 66 — a 516-mile loop around the Highlands starting and finishing in Inverness. But which direction should you ride it? It's one of the most debated questions in UK motorcycle touring, and the answer depends on what you value most.

The Case for Clockwise (East Coast First)

Riding clockwise means heading up the east coast first, through Easter Ross and Caithness, before turning west at Durness and descending the dramatic west coast. Most organised tours and the official NC500 marketing suggest this direction.

  • Build-up effect — The east coast is beautiful but the west coast is jaw-dropping. Saving the best for later creates a crescendo of scenery
  • Bealach na Bà descent — You'll descend the famous pass towards Applecross with views over Skye
  • Against the sun — Afternoon light illuminates the west coast mountains beautifully
  • Follow the majority — Most motorhomes go anticlockwise, so clockwise puts you against them on single-track roads (arguable benefit)

The Case for Anticlockwise (West Coast First)

Going anticlockwise means tackling the stunning west coast immediately. You'll hit Applecross, Torridon, and Durness in the first few days while you're fresh and enthusiastic.

  • Best scenery first — If weather closes in later, you've already bagged the highlights
  • Bealach na Bà ascent — Climbing the pass is arguably more exciting than descending it
  • Less traffic — The majority of NC500 traffic goes clockwise, so anticlockwise can feel quieter
  • Morning light on the west — Early starts are rewarded with soft morning light on the mountains
Our recommendation: Go anticlockwise. The west coast deserves your freshest riding, and climbing the Bealach na Bà is more thrilling than descending it. But honestly, both directions are magnificent.

Does It Really Matter?

Truthfully, the NC500 is spectacular in both directions. The road is the same — the same mountains, lochs, and single-track sections. What changes is the order and the light. If you're riding in summer with long days and stable weather, the direction barely matters. If you have limited time or unpredictable weather, go anticlockwise to prioritise the west coast.

Practical Considerations

Whichever direction you choose, book accommodation in advance for Durness, Ullapool, and Applecross — these are pinch points with limited beds. Carry cash as some remote establishments don't take cards. Fill up at every fuel station on the west coast. And leave extra time — the single-track roads on the west coast are slow but spectacular. keyTakeaways: The NC500 is a 516-mile loop around the Highlands starting and finishing in Inverness.
Clockwise rides the east coast first, saving the dramatic west coast for a scenic crescendo.
Anticlockwise tackles the west coast, Applecross and the Bealach na Ba ascent early while you are fresh.
Most traffic and motorhomes travel clockwise, so anticlockwise can feel quieter on the single-track sections.
Book accommodation ahead at Durness, Ullapool and Applecross, and fill up at every west coast fuel station.

faq.q: Should I ride the NC500 clockwise or anticlockwise?
faq.a: Both directions are magnificent as the road, mountains and lochs are identical. Our recommendation is anticlockwise so the spectacular west coast gets your freshest riding and you climb the Bealach na Ba rather than descend it. If weather closes in later, you will already have ridden the highlights.

In summer with long days and stable weather, the direction barely matters. What changes is the order of the scenery and the quality of the light. If you have limited time or unpredictable weather, go anticlockwise to prioritise the west coast early in your trip.

faq.q: Where should I book accommodation in advance?
faq.a: Durness, Ullapool and Applecross are the main pinch points with limited beds, so book these ahead whichever direction you ride. Carry cash as some remote establishments do not take cards, and fill up at every fuel station on the west coast where options are sparse.

faq.q: How long is the NC500 and where does it start?
faq.a: The North Coast 500 is a 516-mile loop around the Highlands that starts and finishes in Inverness. Most riders take between three and seven days, and leaving extra time is wise because the single-track roads on the west coast are slow but spectacular.
